items.title: Edit nav and footer in one place
items.summary: The site name, built-in links, custom links and footer text live in one settings section.

items.title: Visual header and footer editor
items.summary: Edit the header and footer on a live preview.

items.title: Per-page custom CSS with preview
items.summary: Style one page without touching the rest; preview before saving.

items.title: Public polish bundles
items.summary: Subtle voice and surfaces, status LED, currently-building strip, empty states, restyled 404, tuned light theme.

items.title: Study popup
items.summary: Opens filling the window, movable and resizable.

items.title: Study weak spots
items.summary: Remembers what each person misses and builds a question set from it.

items.title: SEO metadata quality reports
items.summary: Site Health flags thin, duplicate or missing titles and descriptions.

items.title: Sitemap and noindex controls
items.summary: "Exclude from sitemap" and a real noindex option, each explained in the editor.

items.title: Future-date preview
items.summary: See what the site looks like on a date in the future (scheduled posts).

items.title: Footer RSS and Share links
items.summary: Every page footer now ends with an RSS feed link and a Share this page button that opens the share sheet or copies the link. The button only appears where it can work.

items.title: Site quality passes: SEO, bugs, layout, spacing and UX (public site)
items.summary: Three rounds over every public page on desktop and phone, in both themes: nav highlight alignment, active tab kept in view, a better RSS feed, a styled slow-down page, tap-target sizes, and long text, titles and tags no longer stretching phone pages sideways. One-item topic pages stay out of search. The audit now reports 0 high and 0 medium findings.

items.title: Reading completion per article
items.summary: Analytics has a Read to the end list: for each article and project, the share of visits that scrolled to the end and stayed long enough to have read it (40% of the reading time its length suggests). Anonymous, nothing stored in the visitor's browser, your own visits and crawlers not counted.

items.title: Contact form and inbox
items.summary: A form visitors can use, and an inbox in the admin.
items.notes: Needs a new database table and stores visitors' personal data, so it needs your go-ahead.

items.title: Pin Mermaid and add integrity checks
items.summary: Stop loading diagram code from a CDN at whatever version it likes: pin the version with an integrity hash, or host it ourselves.
items.notes: Pinning is quick; hosting it ourselves makes the site fully self-contained. Which do you prefer?

items.title: Cache public pages at the edge
items.summary: Serve public HTML from Cloudflare's cache for speed.

items.title: Redesigned Add Block palette and article editor groups
items.summary: Blocks and article fields grouped so they are quicker to find.

items.title: Block inspector overhaul
items.summary: Grouped, searchable controls with per-control reset.

items.title: One button and control system
items.summary: The same buttons and controls, editable from settings, across the admin and the public site.

items.title: Admin density setting
items.summary: Compact or comfortable spacing.

items.title: Design tokens
items.summary: Shared spacing and shadow scales.

items.title: Dashboard home
items.summary: Counts, recent activity and flags on one screen.

items.title: Canvas improvements
items.summary: Real block previews, a selection toolbar with an Edit button, rescaling, minimum sizes, blocks that never clip their content.

items.title: Block grouping and reusable sections
items.summary: Group blocks, save a group as a section, insert it on any page.

items.title: Bulk actions everywhere
items.summary: Select several songs, simulations, scans, redirects, trash items or media and act on them together.

items.title: Media Library filters
items.summary: Filter by dimensions, duplicates and folder.

items.title: Resizable side panels and dialogs
items.summary: Drag panels to size them and hide them; dialogs resize by their sides.

items.title: Save indicators and Ctrl+S
items.summary: The same "saved" feedback in every editor; Ctrl/Cmd+S saves the one on top.

items.title: Accessibility pass
items.summary: Axe findings fixed across the admin and the public site.

items.title: Command palette
items.summary: Ctrl+K to jump to anything.

items.title: Pre-publish checklist
items.summary: Before an article goes live it lists what is worth fixing (title length, thin text, missing alt text, broken links...) and lets you publish anyway.

items.title: Scripts window
items.summary: Write small scripts against the site in a code editor; preview what they would change, then apply.
items.notes: A sandboxed runner with a helper library, starter templates and a list of every helper. Changing one site setting leaves the others alone.

items.title: Features board
items.summary: To do on the left (bugs, things that need attention, almost-done work, ideas, decisions waiting on you), Working on now and Done on the right. You add your own requests; Claude moves items across as they are started and finished.
items.notes: Your requests live on the site: use Copy for Claude to paste the new ones into the chat so they can be picked up.

items.title: Node-based visual editor
items.summary: Build automations by wiring nodes together, like Unreal Blueprints, inside the Scripts window. Starts with CSS: swap a colour on every page, add a rule to every page, set the accent colour, restyle blocks. It compiles to code you can read, and runs through the same Preview then Apply as Scripts.
items.notes: Same limits as Scripts: it automates content, CSS and settings work. New block types or tools still need code. More nodes come as you ask for them.

items.title: Plugins: custom blocks from a template
items.summary: Define a new block type from an HTML/CSS template plus settings fields.
items.notes: The one remaining part of the plugin idea that looks worth doing.

items.title: Scripts that run on a schedule or for visitors
items.summary: Run a script nightly, or run code on public pages.
items.notes: Not recommended: it means code acting without you watching, or on your visitors' browsers.

items.title: Trash for media files and scans
items.summary: Deleted media and scans go to Trash first, like pages and articles.
items.notes: How long should deleted files stay in Trash, and should their older versions go with them?

items.title: Two-factor sign-in (TOTP)
items.summary: An authenticator-app code on top of the password.
items.notes: Do you want it, and should it be asked for every sign-in or remembered per device?

Identical gates share one table, custom tables are marked, and it reads on a phone and with a screen reader (the old hover text never did).

items.summary: 58 Playwright tests, run in parallel on throwaway servers (about 3 minutes), reporting only new failures.

items.title: CLAUDE.md
items.summary: The site's layout, workflow and rules written down so every session starts fast.

items.title: Fix the remaining known-failing browser tests
items.summary: All four browser tests that were failing for old reasons now pass (the media library one no longer depends on seeded folders, the others learned about the in-page dialogs and folded sections), and two of them no longer exit 0 after printing FAIL. A full run is now clean with nothing set aside.

items.title: Pick a share picture and a fuller home page title
items.summary: Links to the site show no picture, and the home page's search title is just "Dominick".
items.notes: Two quick choices only you can make: upload a default share image in Settings > Sharing (1200 x 630 works best), and say if you want a longer home page title such as your name plus what the site is. I can write the title once you pick the wording.

items.title: Admin console quality pass
items.summary: Every admin tool, tab, editor and dropdown checked on desktop and phone in both themes. Fixed: keyboard focus lost after the Diagnostics scan and after closing a builder, unlabelled journal fields, scrolling log lists the keyboard could not reach, low-contrast accent buttons and error text in light and dark, and phone-sized tap targets and a squeezed image-address field. A new audit script re-checks all of it in about four minutes.

items.title: Song Studio
items.summary: The only way to make a song now, built for a phone first, drawn from your sketch: five fixed tracks stacked on top of each other (1 Drums, 2 Bass, 3 Chords, 4 Melody, 5 Lead) that you scroll through or tap, the open track's card with a strip of bars, Steps or a Roll to draw notes (drag to hold a note, drag to erase), play controls with volume and metronome buttons that pop up their sliders, and a piano that stays at the bottom. A Tools sheet holds everything else the old editor could do: each track's sound and its shape (attack, release, brightness, vibrato and more), the track tools, the song's settings, patterns and song order, the player look and every export. Songs are stored as before.

items.title: Song length, track loops and free recording
items.summary: A song has a number of bars (or grows as you record) and every track has its own strip of bars: a two-bar drum beat can loop under everything while you record a melody for as long as you like, a bar can be made different from the ones it repeats, and Loop can be turned off per track. Up to 16 patterns and 64 bars. The public player, audio, stems and MIDI file follow it.

items.title: Free or scale-snapped notes, sound shaping, MIDI keyboard, default tempo
items.summary: Notes are free by default; pick a scale and turn on Snap and what you play or tap moves to the nearest note of it. Every melodic track can shape its sound (attack, decay, sustain, release, brightness, thickness, vibrato, wave) and the tweaks are saved with the song. A MIDI keyboard connects from the top bar (and reconnects by itself); on Drums its pads play and record the drum sounds. Site Settings has a Songs tab for the tempo, length and drum kit a new song starts with.

items.title: Song module upgrades
items.summary: Better melody instruments, more drum sounds, echo, chord progressions, and several patterns chained into a full song, all shipped one by one. Old songs sound exactly the same.

items.title: Melody instruments
items.summary: Pick Pluck, Lead, Pad, Bass or Bell for the melody; each shapes the note with its own attack, release and filter. Old songs keep their plain sound.

items.title: Held notes survive import and MIDI export
items.summary: Importing a song file used to drop its held (tied) notes, and the MIDI file wrote them as separate short notes. Both now keep them as one long note.

items.title: More drum sounds
items.summary: Open hat, rim, tom and crash in all three kits, added from a menu under the grid and removed with the ×. A closed hat cuts a ringing open hat. Three new starter beats use them. They export to MIDI, stems and song files.

items.title: Echo
items.summary: A tempo-synced echo slider next to Space: repeats a dotted eighth later, each one quieter and duller. Off by default, in exports and on the public player.

items.title: Chord progressions
items.summary: Stamp a whole progression (pop, doo-wop, jazz, minor, Andalusian, canon and more) in any key across the loop, held so the chords ring, in one undo step. The key follows the highlighted scale.

items.title: Import a MIDI file
items.summary: Songs list → Import MIDI…: drums land on the drum rows, the busiest other part becomes the melody (moved by octaves to fit, long notes tied), and each bar becomes a pattern with a song order. It makes a new song and tells you what could not be kept (tempo changes, other time signatures, unknown drums, extra parts, bars past 32). Export MIDI now writes the whole song order too.

items.title: Bar counter on the player
items.summary: A song with a song order now says "6 bars" at rest and "Bar 3 of 6" while it plays, with a thin segment per bar (done, now, to come). The builder's preview shows the same plus the pattern letter. One-bar songs show nothing.

items.title: Bass line
items.summary: A second part under the melody: press Bass above the piano roll for its own low roll (C1 to B2), bass sound (or pluck, lead, pad, bell), volume, mute and hide. It has its own notes in every pattern, the same shift, reverse, random, tie, arpeggio and transpose tools, chord roots from a progression, and Follow the kick. It plays on the public player, in the audio and stems, in the MIDI file (own track, channel 2) and in the report. Importing a MIDI file puts a part named Bass, or one below C3, on it. Songs that never use it are unchanged.

items.title: Starter songs
items.summary: The New song menu now lists four complete little songs to start from or learn from: Lo-fi loop, Four on the floor, Funk groove and Dark trap. Each has patterns, a song order, a melody, a bass line and mix settings, with notes on how it is built.

items.title: Move bars in the song order, [ and ] for patterns
items.summary: Every bar in the song order has Earlier and Later buttons, so a pattern can go anywhere (add it, then move it). While editing, [ and ] open the previous and next pattern.

items.title: Hidden Notes
items.summary: A private tab only you can see: Hidden Notes appears in the nav when you are signed in and opens a page where you keep writings, with search, autosave and lock. Notes are sealed in your browser with a passphrase, so the site and its database only hold scrambled text; there is no reset if you forget it. It is left out of backups and survives a restore; a sealed copy can be downloaded and imported, the passphrase can be changed, and it locks itself after ten idle minutes.

items.title: Pump
items.summary: A Pump slider next to Echo: the music (melody, bass, chords and lead) dips on every kick and swells back, like sidechain compression, so the groove breathes. Off by default; it is in the audio export, the waveform and on the public player. The house starter uses it.

items.title: Drum fills, and copy a part from another pattern
items.summary: Add fill changes the end of a bar into a snare roll, snare build, tom run, kick-and-snare drive or a drop-out. In a song with several patterns, Copy here takes the drums, melody, bass line or everything from another pattern into the open one.

items.title: Patterns and song order
items.summary: Up to four patterns (A to D) per song, switched with buttons, copied or removed, and a song order (like A A B A C) that plays them one after another. Play can follow the order or loop the pattern you're editing. The public player, the waveform, audio and stem export and the MIDI file all cover the whole song. Old songs are untouched.

items.title: More sounds, deeper sound editing, recording helpers
items.summary: Over forty instruments in six groups and fifteen drum kits. The Sound tab now has an envelope, a filter (type, brightness, resonance, sweep), tone (voices, thickness, sub, noise, drive, FM) and movement (vibrato and tremolo, with speeds), and each drum sound has its own tune, length and tone. Preview works on every sound, and Play and Preview no longer go silent on a phone that was keeping the sound asleep. Next to Rec: a button that always records from the beginning, Quantize (nearest step, eighth or beat) and a Follow switch for the editor.

items.title: Blocks look the same wherever they are placed
items.summary: A block is exactly its content: no stray outer margins from paragraphs, headings or rules, so the space between blocks is the same for every kind, 16px on a phone and 8px on a wide screen. A spacer keeps its height on a phone (it used to vanish), and nothing runs past the screen edge.

items.title: Studio has its own page and nav tab
items.summary: The Studio is now a page of its own, /studio, with a Studio tab in the nav, open to everyone. The song builder fills the page; visitors make songs that are kept in their own browser (nothing is sent to the site), and can save and share song files. It follows the site's light and dark.

items.title: The admin opens on the page: click where you want a block
items.summary: The admin opens on the page itself with the page chooser and + Add in the top bar. Click an empty spot on the page and pick a block: it lands right there (pushing what is below it down). A selected block has Size (a quarter to full width, left, centre or right), Settings and Edit in its toolbar. The menu and the inspector stay tucked away until you ask: ☰ Tools and Settings.

items.title: Page editor: the rest of the Squarespace feel
items.summary: Next: blocks in the editor that look exactly like the live page, insert bars between blocks on a phone, and folding the inspector into the selection bar.
items.notes: Tell me what feels off in the new click-to-add flow and I will fix that first.

items.title: One chunky look for every button and field
items.summary: Buttons are now a thick outline with a flat fill and a hard shadow they sink into when pressed, on the site, in the admin and in the Studio. Text fields have the same thick outline, and a labelled field can carry its label in the outline. Site Settings > Buttons & controls has a Chunky choice (the new default) next to the old looks.

items.title: Dials, a menu card for adding blocks, and the Studio fan
items.summary: Sliders in the Studio are now glowing rotary dials you drag up and down. Click-to-add on a page opens a rounded menu card with the blocks and page settings. The Studio's bottom bar has a Rec button: tap to record, hold it to fan out volume, metronome, undo, redo, stop, clear, start-from-top, quantize and follow.

items.title: Fewer tabs, and tab changes that slide
items.summary: Random and Hidden Notes are no longer tabs (articles and Hidden Notes are in the finder). A page with Study on it stays out of the nav and search engines, is found with the site's search, and always asks for the password. Moving between tabs slides the page like a carousel with no reload, the Studio and the song and circuit players included.

items.title: A finder instead of header buttons
items.summary: The header is just the nav dial; its last stop is Search, which opens a Spotlight-like finder: type to search the site, or find a setting (light or dark, reduce motion, text size), a section, Surprise me, Saved or History. Press / or Ctrl+K to open it anywhere.

items.title: Tabs switch with no wait, and no site name in the header
items.summary: Every page of the nav is kept once it has been fetched, so a tab shows straight away and a fresh copy is fetched quietly in the background. The Studio's editor is fetched ahead of time too, so the Studio tab opens without loading. The header is just the nav dial now, centred.

items.title: The Studio is part of the site, not the admin's editor on top
items.summary: /studio opens on a shelf of your songs: New song, the starter songs, opening a song or MIDI file, and a card per song with a little picture of its tracks, a Play button right on the card, Copy and Delete. The editor opens right there under the site's nav, in the site's look, with no frame or dialog around it; Songs takes you back to the shelf and keeps what you did. Switching to another tab and back slides in place and the song you had open is still open.

items.title: Studio: the ⋯ controls as a row, quantize shows its value
items.summary: Holding Rec (or the ⋯) lays a row of buttons over the play bar instead of a half circle over the steps, without labels. Quantize shows 1/16, 1/8, 1/4 or Off and a tap moves to the next.

items.title: Camera-dial nav and browser-style menus
items.summary: The nav is a camera dial: an icon over each name, a ruler of ticks and a glowing needle under the page you are on that turns to whatever you point at. The header is one row from a tablet up and slim on the Studio page. Menus in the admin and Site Settings are plain cards with quiet rows and thin lines between groups, and Site Settings has its sections down the left.

items.title: The Studio is no longer crammed on a phone
items.summary: The five tracks are one row of tabs, the open track has one row of controls, the steps or roll fill the rest of the screen (half a bar of drum steps at a time with a pager), and Play, Stop, Undo, Rec and the keys are always in reach. The fan has names under its circles, the Tools sheet has its own Play button, a phone on its side gets two columns, and a wide screen shows the tracks as a rail. A new song on /studio is kept from its first change.

items.title: Fixes from a full review of the site and the admin
items.summary: Size > Full and the phone's up/down arrows no longer put blocks on top of each other; the canvas redraws when a panel opens or closes; Focus mode no longer blocks + Add; the quick editor no longer covers the block's toolbar; delete buttons are red; fields have a clear outline; nav dropdowns show; articles open with the text (sharing moved below it); /search has its own box; trailing slashes go to one address; Saved and History are kept out of search engines.
